welcome.title: Getting started: check {product} works for you
welcome.body:
{product} is connected. Four steps, about five minutes:

1. Ask your AI: "Which of my machines can you reach?" It calls `machines` and lists each machine and whether it is online.
2. On your phone, open {hub}/approvals. Tap **Notify this phone**, then **Send me a test approval**. Approve it from the notification.
3. Ask your AI for something small on one machine, for example: "Show me the free disk space on <machine>." Anything you should sign off on waits for you on your phone.
4. Tell your AI it worked, and ask it to close this ticket.

Stuck on a step? Tell your AI which one; it can read this ticket.

operator.title: Operator
operator.account_link: You run this hub: let people in and set their plans on the [operator page](/operator).
operator.status_open: Sign-up is **open**: everyone who connects is let in at once.
operator.status_early_access: Sign-up is **early access**: everyone who connects waits here until you let them in.
operator.how_to_change: To change it, set `early_access.mode` in the site's `site.json` to `open` or `early_access`, then run `hub-up.sh --site DIR --site-only`. Once it is open, people waiting are let in on their next request; nobody already in is ever put back.
operator.done_admitted: Let in: {n}. Their next call works.
operator.none_picked: Nobody was checked: check the people to let in, then press the button.
operator.not_from_here: That came from another site, so nothing was changed. Use the operator page itself.
operator.admitted_empty: Nobody has been let in yet.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.operator_link: How people find and use this hub: [analytics](/operator/analytics).
analytics.intro: Counted by this hub itself, as it serves its pages: no cookie, no script, nothing third-party. A visitor counts once a day, so the same person on two days counts twice.
analytics.off: This hub counts nothing: `analytics.enabled` is false in its config (or `DEVAGOTCHI_HUB_ANALYTICS=off`).
analytics.kept: Raw visits are kept {days} days; the daily totals are kept.
analytics.dropped: {n} records were not kept because the hub's queue was full.
analytics.chart_title: Visitors and page views per day
analytics.chart_summary: {views} page views and {visitors} visitors over {n} days.
analytics.funnel_intro: Visitors over these {n} days, and the accounts made in them: how far each got so far.
analytics.active: Active, with a command run: **{week}** in the last 7 days, **{month}** in the last 30.

workflow.dead_text: It expired, or what it was for was cancelled. Ask your AI for a new one: it takes it a moment.
workflow.finished: All done. Go back to your AI: it carries on from here.
workflow.keep_text: Your AI made this account for you when you connected it, and nothing signs you in to it yet. Add a sign-in now to keep it and see your machines from anywhere. Optional: everything above works without it.
workflow.keep_done: Your account is kept: sign in from anywhere with what you just added.
workflow.command_note: Paste it on that machine as is. It works once, for 15 minutes; pressing the button again gives a new one and the old one stops working.
workflow.name_label: Its name (lowercase letters, digits and dashes)

os_hint.docker: Paste it into a terminal on a Linux machine with Docker Compose and press Enter.
os_hint.host: Paste it into a root shell on the Proxmox or Incus host itself (not inside a guest) and press Enter.
os_hint.linux: Paste it into a terminal on the machine and press Enter; sudo may ask for your password.
os_hint.windows: Open PowerShell (Start, type PowerShell, Enter), paste it and press Enter. No administrator needed.

workflow.mac: **Mac:** not available yet. There is no Mac build of {product}, so there is nothing to install on one.
workflow.no_downloads: This hub hands out no builds, so it has no one-line install to give. Its operator can turn that on.
workflow.no_build_for: This hub has no {os} build to hand out yet, so there is no line for it.
workflow.no_push: This hub sends no notifications, so there is no phone to turn on here.
workflow.notify: Turn on notifications on this phone
workflow.phone_hint: On a computer now? Open this same link on your phone and press the button there.
workflow.refused: That came from another site, so nothing was changed. Use the button on this page.

claude.name: Claude
claude.how: **On claude.ai or in the Claude desktop app:** open **Customize**, then **Connectors**, press **Add custom connector**, paste the address below, press **Add**, then **Connect** on it. **In Claude Code:** run the command below in a terminal, start `claude`, type `/mcp`, choose it and press **Authenticate**. The Free plan holds one custom connector.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.how: **In ChatGPT on the web** (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Education): open **Settings**, then **Apps**, turn on **Developer mode** under **Advanced settings**, press **Create app**, paste the address below as its MCP server, choose **OAuth**, and connect. **In Codex:** run the command below; it opens the sign-in itself.

grok.name: Grok
grok.how: **On grok.com:** open [grok.com/connectors](https://grok.com/connectors), press **New Connector**, choose **Custom**, paste the address below and finish its sign-in. On a Business or Enterprise team, an admin adds the connector first.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.how: **In Cursor:** add the entry below to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (every project) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (this project), save, and press **Connect** next to it under **MCP** when Cursor asks you to sign in.

workflow.client_browser: {client} opens a page to connect in your browser. Press the button below in the browser it will open (on a computer, your usual one), so it joins this account instead of making a new one.
workflow.client_ready: This browser will join {client} to your account: when its page asks, press **Connect**.
workflow.client_secured: {client} opens a page to connect: sign in there as you usually do, then press **Connect**.
workflow.qr: This page's link as a QR code: scan it with your phone's camera
